- **ACT:EO:9250>EO:9555**; Scdde89fe080e569e534d0cc9; {"actor_id":"EO:9555","char_end":16661,"char_start":15406,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":15701,"char_start":15545,"text":"The amendments hereby promulgated \nshall become effective on the ninetieth \nday following the date of publication of \nthis order in the F ederal R egister ."},{"char_end":30004,"char_start":29667,"text":"(a) Liberty Incandescent Supply\nCompany, its successors and assigns, \nshall not for a period of four months \nfrom the effective date of this order ap­\nply or extend any preference ratings in \nits purchase of new fluorescent lighting \nfixtures and parts, unless otherwise spe­\ncifically authorized in writing by the War \nProduction Board."},{"char_end":30645,"char_start":30583,"text":"(d) This order shall take effect on \nthe 25th day of May 1945."},{"char_end":95481,"char_start":95085,"text":"=== PDF page 13 of 96 ===\n6067FEDERAL REGISTER, Saturday, May 26, 1945\nRevised Maximum Price Regulation 434 \nRevised Maximum Price Regulation 467 \nMaximum Price Regulation 481 \nMaximum Price Regulation 483 \nMaximum Price Regulation 485 \nMaximum Price Regulation 520 \nMaximum Price Regulation 524 \nMaximum Price Regulation 525\nThis Supplementary Order No. 112 \nshall become effective May 30, 1945."},{"char_end":96869,"char_start":96207,"text":"The adoption in the Territory \nof Hawaii of gasoline rationing regula­\ntions modeled on those in effect on the \nmainland, but modified to suit peculiarly \nlocal conditions, goes hand in hand with \nthe adoption of this ration order which \nis designed to do in Hawaii what has \nalready been done on the mainland: \nnamely, the preservation of tire carcasses \nthrough a liberal recapping policy, and \nthe rationing of new and used tires on \nthe basis of the applicant’ s importance \nto the war effort and public need, as \nevidenced by his driving requirements \nand gasoline allotments.\n§  1315.19 Mileage rationing; t i r e  \nregulations for the Territory of Hawaii."},{"char_end":100023,"char_start":99795,"text":"(a) No provision of this order \nshall affect the validity or valid period \nof any certificate issued pursuant to a \ntire ration order in effect on any of the \nislands of the Territory prior to the effec­\ntive date of this order."},{"char_end":100321,"char_start":100024,"text":"(b) All certificates issued pursuant to \nany other tire ration order previously \nin effect in the Territory which are valid \nafter the effective date of this order, \nshall be subject to the same restrictions, \nprohibitions and conditions of use as \nthough they were issued pursuant to this \norder."},{"char_end":100775,"char_start":100452,"text":"Territory of Hawaii, and all other orders \nrationing tires in the Territory of \nHawaii: Provided, however,  That any \nviolations which occurred prior to the ef­\nfective date of this revised ration order \nshall be governed by the orders, regula­\ntions and amendments thereto, in effect \nat the time such violations occurred."},{"char_end":131923,"char_start":131581,"text":"(ii) If a respondent against whom an \norder has been issued for failure to ap­\npear at the hearing shows, within a rea­\nsonable time not to exceed five (5) days \nfrom the effective date of such order, \ngood cause to the Board for such failure, \nthe Board may set aside such order and \ngrant the respondent a full hearing on \nthe charges made."},{"char_end":132387,"char_start":132173,"text":"The Board shall fix the ef­\nfective date of such order except that \nif it fails to do so such order shall be­\ncome effective 24 hours after personal \nservice or delivery by mail as evidenced \nby the return receipt."},{"char_end":133083,"char_start":132813,"text":"(b) Any person against whom an \norder has been issued pursuant to the \nprovisions of paragraph (a) may within \nfifteen (15) days after the effective date \nthereof, appeal from such order by fil­\ning a statement of objections to the \norder with the Board which issued it."},{"char_end":135471,"char_start":135214,"text":"(2) Upon the vehicle on which it was \nmounted on August 1, 1943: Provided, \nThat at the time the tires were mounted \non the vehicle such mounting was not in \nviolation of any previous tire or gasoline \nrationing regulations then in effect in \nthe territory."},{"char_end":158804,"char_start":158789,"text":"Effective date."},{"char_end":158854,"char_start":158806,"text":"This order shall be­\ncome effective May 30,1945."},{"char_end":167041,"char_start":166425,"text":"ARTICLE VI— EXPIRATION AND REVOCATION OF \nRATIONS\n6.1 Surrender of expired coupons.\n6.2 Expiration of rations.\n6.3 Expiration of rations upon cessation of\nuse or change in ownership.\n6.4 Denial of gasoline rations.\n6.5 Coupon books property of Office of\nPrice Administration; revocations.\n6.6 Revocation, suspension, and denial of\nconsumer’ s ration after hearing.\n6.7 Effective period of order revoking ra­\ntion and of declaration of ineligi­\nbility.\n6.8 Presentation of registration cards and\ntire inspection records after revoca­\ntion of ration or denial of rations for \na specified period and notations \nthereon."},{"char_end":175276,"char_start":175005,"text":"All rations issued pursuant to Ration \nOrder No. 5B which shall remain in effect \nafter the effective date of this Order, \nshall be subject to the same restrictions, \nprohibitions and conditions of use as \nthough they were issued pursuant to \nRevised Ration Order No. 5E."},{"char_end":270058,"char_start":269515,"text":"(a) A Board, after hearing, may \nrevoke, cancel or suspend the ration, or \nrations of a person in whole or in part, \nand in such a case require the surrender \nto it of coupons, coupon books or other \nration evidences to the extent required to \nmake such revocation, cancellation or \nsuspension effective, may deny a ration \nor rations in whole or in part and for \nsuch period as the Board may deem ap­\npropriate in the public interest, where a \nperson has violated any of the provisions \nof Revised Ration Order IB or Revised \nRation Order 5E."},{"char_end":271313,"char_start":270524,"text":"If the respondent ad­\nmits the charge or fails to appear at the \nhearing, or if the Board determines after \nhearing that the respondent has com­\nmitted any of the acts or violations with\n*  which he is charged, the Board may by \norder revoke, cancel and suspend for a \nperiod which shall be stated therein, the \nrations issued to him in whole or in \npart and direct him to surrender to it \nthe coupons, coupon books or other ra­\ntion evidences issued to him to the ex­\ntent required to make such revocation \neffective, and the Board may by order \ndeny him a ration or rations in whole or \nin part for such period as the Board may \ndeem appropriate in the public interest\n(2) If a respondent against whom an \norder has been issued for failure to ap­\npear at the hearing shows, within a rea-"},{"char_end":271632,"char_start":271315,"text":"=== PDF page 33 of 96 ===\n6087FEDERAL REGISTER, Saturday, May 26, 1945\nsonable time not to exceed thirty days \nfrom the effective date of such order, \ngood cause to the Board for such failure, \nthe Board may cancel or order the stay \nof such order and shall grant the re­\nspondent a full hearing on the charges \nmade."},{"char_end":272186,"char_start":271876,"text":"The Board, in its discretion, shall fix the \neffective date of such order except that \nif the Board fails to fix such effective \ndate such order shall, if personally \nserved, become effective at the time of \nsuch service, and if served by registered \nmail, on the date of delivery shown on \nthe return receipt."},{"char_end":272908,"char_start":272617,"text":"(b) Any person against whom an or­\nder has been issued pursuant to the \nprovisions of paragraph (a) of this sec­\ntion, may, within fifteen (15) days after \nthe effective date thereof, appeal from \nsuch order by filing a statement of ob­\njections to the order with the Board \nwhich issued it."},{"char_end":273659,"char_start":273568,"text":"Sec. 6.7 Effective Period of order re­\nvoking ration and of declaration of in­\neligibility."},{"char_end":275317,"char_start":274657,"text":"Whenever by an order issued \npursuant to the provisions of Revised \nRation Order No. 5E a ration of a per­\nson is revoked, cancelled or suspended in \nwhole or in part, or a person has been de­\nnied a ration for a specified period, pur­\nsuant to section 6.6 (a) or such an order \nhas been modified or nullified, such per­\nson shall, within twenty-four (24) hours \nafter such order becomes effective, pre­\nsent the Tire Inspection Record and the \nregistration card or registration certifi­\ncate, if any, of any motor vehicle affected \nby any such order to the Board or repre­\nsentative of the Office of Price Admin­\nistration that issued or modified such \norder."},{"char_end":309546,"char_start":309531,"text":"Effective date."},{"char_end":309610,"char_start":309548,"text":"This revised ration \norder shall become effective May 30,1945."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:9250>EO:9555","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["This order, as amended, shall not affect \nany liabilities incurred for violation of \nthis order, or.of actions taken by the War \nProduction Board under this order, be­\nfore its amendment.","In adopting this \nregulation it has been necessary not only \nto take into consideration the necessity \nfor saving rubber, but also the fact that \nall rubber and gasoline must be imported \ninto the Territory of Puerto Rico by \nwater, thus making it necessary to con­\nsider the question of transportation as \naffected by world conditions."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1945-05-24","target_id":"EO:9250","verb":"amend"}

assist in the maximum produc­\ntion of goods and services required to \nmeet domestic and foreign needs, (1) by \nassuring assistance in making available \nmaterials and supplies required for the \nproduction of such goods and services;\n(2) by providing assistance to the con­\nversion and utilization of war plants and \nfacilities, both privately and publicly \nowned; and (3) by providing effective \njob placement assistance to war workers \nand returning service men and women."},{"char_end":4492,"char_start":3495,"text":"The departments and agencies of \nthe Government shall take vigorous, con­\ncerted and uniform action toward these \nends and pursuant to this Order, under \nthe guidance and direction of the Direc­\ntor of War Mobilization and Recon­\nversion.\nn\nDuring the transition to a free econ­\nomy, the Secretary of Agriculture, the \nFederal Loan Administrator, and the Di­\nrector of Economic Stabilization shall \nnot only take all measures required by \nlaw to support prices but shall take such \nfurther measures authorized by law as \nmay be necessary to prevent any collapse \nof values or discouragement of the full \nand effective use of productive resources.\nn i\nThe Price Administrator, and in the \nexercise of his price responsibilities un­\nder the law the Secretary of Agriculture, \nshall, subject to such directives provided \nfor by law as may be issued by the Eco­\nnomic Stabilization Director, take all \nnecessary steps to assure that the cost \nof living and the general level of prices \nshall not rise."},{"char_end":4882,"char_start":4493,"text":"Subject to such author­\nity, the Price Administrator and, in the \nexercise of his price responsibilities un­\nder the law, the Secretary of {"actor_id":"EO:9600","char_end":247239,"char_start":246570,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2784,"char_start":2309,"text":"To assist in the maximum produc­\ntion of goods and services required to \nmeet domestic and foreign needs, (1) by \nassuring assistance in making available \nmaterials and supplies required for the \nproduction of such goods and services;\n(2) by providing assistance to the con­\nversion and utilization of war plants and \nfacilities, both privately and publicly \nowned; and (3) by providing effective \njob placement assistance to war workers \nand returning service men and women."},{"char_end":4492,"char_start":3495,"text":"The departments and agencies of \nthe Government shall take vigorous, con­\ncerted and uniform action toward these \nends and pursuant to this Order, under \nthe guidance and direction of the Direc­\ntor of War Mobilization and Recon­\nversion.\nn\nDuring the transition to a free econ­\nomy, the Secretary of Agriculture, the \nFederal Loan Administrator, and the Di­\nrector of Economic Stabilization shall \nnot only take all measures required by \nlaw to support prices but shall take such \nfurther measures authorized by law as \nmay be necessary to prevent any collapse \nof values or discouragement of the full \nand effective use of productive resources.\nn i\nThe Price Administrator, and in the \nexercise of his price responsibilities un­\nder the law the Secretary of Agriculture, \nshall, subject to such directives provided \nfor by law as may be issued by the Eco­\nnomic Stabilization Director, take all \nnecessary steps to assure that the cost \nof living and the general level of prices \nshall not rise."},{"char_end":4882,"char_start":4493,"text":"Subject to such author­\nity, the Price Administrator and, in the \nexercise of his price responsibilities un­\nder the law, the Secretary of - **ACT:EO:9250>EO:9651**; S6a6c4904acf66c5859597429; {"actor_id":"EO:9651","char_end":3665,"char_start":0,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":884,"char_start":410,"text":"The Stabilization Administrator, designated pursuant to Executive Order No. 9620 of September 20, 1945, shall approve, under section 2 of part IV of this order, a wage or salary increase falling into any of the following three classes in any case in which such increase has been found by the National War Labor Board or other designated agency to be necessary to correct a maladjustment or inequity which would interfere with the effective transition to a peacetime economy:"},{"char_end":1777,"char_start":1539,"text":"\"The Stabilization Administrator shall continue to approve wage or salary increases approved by the National War Labor Board or other designated agency in cases in which such increases satisfy standards in effect prior to August 18, 1945."},{"char_end":2396,"char_start":2052,"text":"\"Nothing in the foregoing shall be construed to require the National War Labor Board or other designated agency to approve any wage increase unless, in its judgment, the increase is necessary, on the facts of the particular case, to correct a maladjustment or inequity which would interfere with the effective transition to a peacetime economy."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:9250>EO:9651","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. - **ACT:EO:9250>EO:9656**; S690ff34f573f16ac67cf1792; {"actor_id":"EO:9656","char_end":1586,"char_start":699,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1586,"char_start":699,"text":"EXECUTIVE ORDER 9656\nT ransfer  o f S h ip b u il d in g S tabilization  \nC o m m ittee\nBy virtue of the authority vested in me  \nby the Constitution and Statutes, includ­\ning Title I of the First War Powers Act,  \n1941, and as President of the United  \nStates, it is hereby ordered as follows:\nThe Shipbuilding Stabilization Com­\nmittee of the Civilian Production Ad­\nministration, established by General  \nAdministrative Order No. 2-57 of the  \nChairman of the War Production Board,  \neffective August 1,1942, and its functions,  \nincluding those under Executive Order  \nNo. 9250 of October 3,1942, and so much  \nof the records, property, personnel, and  \nfunds of the Civilian Production Admin­\nistration as relates primarily to such  \nfunctions, are transferred to the Depart­\nment of Labor and shall be administered  \nunder the supervision and direction of  \nthe Secretary of Labor."},{"char_end":2189,"char_start":1981,"text":"All prior regulations,  \nrulings, and other directives relating to  \nany function transferred by this order  \nshall remain in effect except as they are  \nhereafter amended or revoked under  \nproper authority."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:9250>EO:9656","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. first invoice after the \neffective date of this order, of the maxi­\nmum prices established by this order for \neach such seller as well as the maximum \nprices established for purchasers upon \nresale, except dealers, including allow­\nable transportation and crating charges."},{"char_end":269745,"char_start":269695,"text":"This order shall become effective April \n25, 1946."},{"char_end":272317,"char_start":271982,"text":"(e) Each seller covered by this order, \nexcept a dealer, shall notify each of his \npurchasers, in writing, at or before the \nissuance of the first invoice after, the \neffective date of this order, of the maxi­\nmum prices established for purchasers \nupon resale, except dealers, including \nallowable transportation and crating \ncharges."},{"char_end":272756,"char_start":272706,"text":"This order shall become effective \nApril 25, 1946."},{"char_end":274812,"char_start":274444,"text":"(e) Each seller covered by this order, \nexcept on sales to consumers, shall notify \neach of his purchasers, in writing, at or \nbefore the issuance of the first, invoice \nafter the effective date of this order, of \nthe maximum prices established by this \norder for each such seller as well as the \nmaximum prices established for pur­\nchasers except dealers upon resale."},{"char_end":275149,"char_start":274813,"text":"(f) Modern Manufacturing Company, \nSeattle, Washington shall print on the \ncarton containing each float valve cov­\nered by this order the following:\nOPA Maximum Retail Price— $ ______\n(Do Not Detach)\n(g) This order may be revoked or \namended by the Price Administrator at \nany time.\n■  This order shall become effective April \n25, 1946."},{"char_end":276943,"char_start":276668,"text":"(d) The maximum prices for sales of \ncutting tools, by resellers, shall be the \nmaximum prices in effect just prior to the \nissuance of this order increased by the \nsame percentage by which their net in­\nvoice cost has been increased by reason \nof the issuance of this order."},{"char_end":277376,"char_start":276944,"text":"(e) All prices established under para­\ngraphs (c) and (d) of this order shall \nbe subject to the same discounts, deduc­\ntions and other allowances in effect to \nany purchasers and classes of purchasers \njust prior to the issuance of this order. -\n(f) Every manufacturer of cutting \ntools shall give written notice to its re­\nsellers of the percentage ampunt by \nwhich this order permits the reseller to \nincrease his maximum prices."},{"char_end":277510,"char_start":277460,"text":"This order\"shall become effective April \n24, 1946."},{"char_end":287051,"char_start":286997,"text":"This amendment shall become effective Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 9.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["Members of the Fed­\neral Reserve System, institutions whose \naccounts are insured by the Federal \nSavings and Loan Insurance Corporation \nand1  institutions whose deposits are in­\nsured by the Federal Deposit Insurance \nCorporation may be approved as mort­\ngagees upon application.\n§ 521,3 Charitable  or nonprofit  \norganizations.","The regula­\ntions in this part may be amended by the \nCommissioner at any time and from \ntime to time, in whole or in part, but \nsuch amendment shall not affect the con­\ntract of insurance on any mortgage al­\nready insured, or any mortgage or pros­\npective mortgage on which the Commis­\nsioner has made a commitment to insure.\n§ 522.19 Effective date."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1946-08-22","target_id":"EO:9250","verb":"amend"}

Express signing-date wording; supplied signing date still needs source confirmation.","provision_label":"Sec. 16.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["Ap- \nlicants further propose, by means of said \nsale and installations, to enable Natural \nGas Company to dispose of equipment \nnow operating uneconomically at a low \nload factor and to replace said facilities \nwith smaller size equipment sufficient to \nhandle available supplies of natural gas, \nthus effecting savings in annual ex­\npenses.","It appearing to the Commission that \na hearing upon the application is neces­\nsary and appropriate:\nIt is ordered, Pursuant to section 4 0  (a) \nof said act, that a public hearing on the \naforesaid application be held on the 27th \nday of September, 1946, at 10:00 a. m ., \neastern daylight saving time, in Room \n318 of the offices of the Securities and Ex­\nchange Commission, 18th and Locust \nStreets, Philadelphia 3, Pennsylvania."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1946-09-23","target_id":"EO:9250","verb":"revoke"}

chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the statutes, and particularly by the First War Powers Act, 1941, and the Act of October 2, 1942, entitled \"An Act to Amend the Emergency Price Control Act of 1942, to Aid in Preventing Inflation, and for Other Purposes,\" as President of the United States and Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy, and in order to safeguard the stabilization of prices, wages, and salaries, affecting the cost of living on the basis of levels existing on September 15, 1942, as authorized and directed by said Act of Congress of October 2, 1942, and Executive Order No. 9250 of October 3, 1942, and to prevent increases in wages, salaries, prices, and profits, which, however justifiable if viewed apart from their effect upon the economy, tend to undermine the basis of stabilization, and to provide such regulations with respect to the control of price, wage, and salary increases as are necessary to maintain stabilization, it is hereby ordered as follows:","sections_touched":["partial"],"signing_date":"1943-04-08","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/209951","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:9328","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 9328—Stabilization of Wages, Prices, and Salaries; Doc. 45-8848; Filed, May 25, 1945; \n10:10 a. m.]\nTITLE 29— LABOR\nChapter VI— National War Labor Board \nP art 803—G eneral O rders\nINCREASES IN  WAGE AND SALARY RATES\nThe National War Labor Board has \namended General Order No. 30 to read \nas follows:\n§  803.30 Increases m wage or salary  \nrates below 55 cents per hour.  In ac­\ncordance with the provisions of section \n4 of Title H of Executive Order 9250, \nincreases in wage or salary rates which \ndo not bring such rates above 55tf per \nhour, may be made without the approval \nof the National War Labor Board. chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the statutes of the United States and particularly the Stabilization Act of 1942 as amended, and for the purpose of carrying out the guiding policies of Executive Order 9599 of August 18, 1945, and amplifying the provisions of part IV thereof, Executive Order 9599 is hereby amended by adding at the end thereof the following part VI:\n\n\"VI.\n\n\"1. The Stabilization Administrator, designated pursuant to Executive Order No. 9620 of September 20, 1945, shall approve, under section 2 of part IV of this order, a wage or salary increase falling into any of the following three classes in any case in which such increase has been found by the National War Labor Board or other designated agency to be necessary to correct a maladjustment or inequity which would interfere with the effective transition to a peacetime economy:\n\n\"a. Increases where the percentage increase in average straight time hourly earnings in the appropriate unit since January 1941 has not equaled the percentage increase in the cost of living between January 1941 and September 1945.\n\n\"b. Increases necessary to correct inequities in wage rates or salaries among plants in the same industry or locality, with due regard to normal competitive relationships.\n\n\"c. Increases necessary to insure full production in an industry, designated by the Stabilization Administrator, which is essential to reconversion and in which existing wage rates or salaries are inadequate to the recruitment of needed manpower.\n\n\"The Stabilization Administrator shall continue to approve wage or salary increases approved by the National War Labor Board or other designated agency in cases in which such increases satisfy standards in effect prior to August 18, 1945.\n\n\"The Stabilization Administrator may define additional classes of wage or salary increases which the National War Labor Board or other designated agency is authorized to approve as necessary to correct a maladjustment or inequity under section 2 or part IV of this order.\n\n\"Nothing in the foregoing shall be construed to require the National War Labor Board or other designated agency to approve any wage increase unless, in its judgment, the increase is necessary, on the facts of the particular case, to correct a maladjustment or inequity which would interfere with the effective transition to a peacetime economy.\n\n\"In making findings under this section the National War Labor Board or other designated agency shall be subject to directives issued by the Stabilization Administrator under the authority conferred by Executive Orders 9250 and 9328 or other applicable Executive Orders.\n\n\"2. Nothing in this order shall be construed to prevent an employer from putting a wage or salary increase into effect and thereafter applying for approval of such increase, under the standards of this order, so that it may be used as the basis for seeking an increase in price ceilings, or for resisting otherwise justifiable reductions in price ceilings, or, in the case of products or services being furnished under contract with a federal procurement agency, for increasing the costs to the United States.\n\n\"3. Notwithstanding the fact that a wage or salary increase has not been approved in accordance with this order, the Price Administrator shall, after the expiration of a reasonable test period, which save in exceptional cases shall be six months after the wage or salary increase has been made, take such increase into account in determining whether an increase in price ceilings is then required under the established standards governing increases in price ceilings.\"\n\nHARRY S. chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(b) of that regulation as being those of  \n“their most closely competitive seller of\nthe same class.” The action effected by  \nthe accompanying amendment will per­\nmit distributors who have already es­\ntablished their March, 1942, maximum  \nprices under §  1499.2 (a) to continue  \nto use those prices but will prohibit dis­\ntributors who could not establish such  \nprices from adopting the high out-of-line  \nprices under §  1499.2 (b ).\nA similar situation existed with respect \nto sales of cane sugar blackstrap molas­\nses and beet sugar final molasses. Re­\nvised Maximum Price Regulation 291  \nestablished the same flat dollars-and-  \ncents prices for both producers and dis­\ntributors, with an option of using a price  \ndetermined under §  1499.2 of the General \nMaximum Price Regulation. Certain „  \nproducers have attempted to exercise  \nthis option by pricing under §  1499.2 (b) \nof the General Maximum Price Regula­\ntion, considering distributors as their  \nmost closely competitive sellers. Dis­\ntributors, because of the functions per­\nformed by them, in general had higher  \nprices in March, 1942 than producers,  \nand it would be disruptive and inequi­\ntable to allow producers to adopt those  \nprices/\" The accompanying amendment  \nremedies this situation by confining a  \nproducer to the flat prices established \nby Revised Maximum Price Regulation  \n291, except when he acts as a distribu­\ntor, in which case he may price as a dis­\ntributor. Distributors may use either  \nthe flat prices established in the regula­\ntion, or they may continue to use the  \nprices established under §  149&.2 (a) of  \nthe General Maximum Price Regulation.  \nThe amendment defines a distributor to  \nclarify the distinction between a dis­\ntributor and a producer, and sets forth  \nconditions under which a producer may  \nprice as a distributor.\nThe amendment also contains a stand­\nard provision requiring notification of  \nnew maximum prices to wholesalers and  \nretailers.\nIn the judgment of the Price Adminis­\ntrator, the action taken by the accom­\npanying amendment is generally fair  \nand equitable and will effectuate the  \npurposes of the Emergency Price Control  \nAct of 1942, as amended, and Executive  \nOrders 9250, 9328, 9599, 9651 and 9697.\n[F R Doc. 46-20601; Filed, Nov. 18, 1946; j r \n11:31a.m.] /\nP art 1351—F ood  and  F ood  P roducts  \n[2d Rev. safety, or interest, but only when all of the conditions \ndescribed in Paragraph 1622.23(a) are found to exist and only if the \nregistrant was classified in Class II-C  prior to the effective date
